items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: Eddie South wanted me to leave this city here when he came here to work with a place called the Moscow Inn... he wanted me to leave here and play violin and clarinet in his band in 1934, which I wouldn't do

ctx.x: The alto saxophone rather rapidly became your principal instrument, didn't it?

Well, it became that because it was the most commercial. So, you always have to follow the dollar sign wherever it goes, if you want to survive and survival was always the name of the game. I would have loved to have been a very good violin player, but there was no survival for me as a violin player because there were just no places for a black violin player to be playing. There was only two of them that I'd ever known that were very famous and that was Atwell Rose and Eddie South. Before that -- as a matter of…

group that had Milt Hinton playing bass in it in 1934 and he wanted me to leave here and play violin and clarinet in his band in 1934, which I wouldn't do because I didn't want to leave Los Angeles. But there was not future for me as a violin player. That's why my uncle gave me the clarinet when I graduated from junior high school and says, "Go out and make some money."
